pass_facts.fact: Current INSPIRE release published 2026-07-05; files update on the first Sunday each month.
London Borough of Barnet is listed on the current release download page.
London Borough of Enfield is listed on the current release download page.
INSPIRE polygons are supplied as separate local-authority GML files.
INSPIRE polygons are an open freehold subset and show indicative property extent rather than legal boundary certainty.
Each INSPIRE polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID relating to a registered title.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary may appear in both local-authority files.
Polygon geometry is captured against British National Grid, EPSG:27700.
Reprojection from British National Grid to WGS84 may shift some features by up to 15 metres.
GML is the supported open-standard exchange format and can be converted by GIS software.

pass_facts.source: HM Land Registry National Polygon technical specification
pass_facts.fact: Poly_ID is a unique polygon reference, Title_No identifies a registered title, all HMLR polygon data is captured in British National Grid, and INSPIRE is a simpler subset.
Direct live title-boundary page reports 2,792,111 records, collector last ran 2026-07-25, new data last found 2026-07-23.
Title-boundary page carries OGL v3 attribution and an explicit caveat that some MHCLG-created data is being replaced by authoritative sources.
The API exposes more than 100 planning and housing datasets through one interface.
latitude and longitude queries return entities whose geometry intersects the supplied point.
Multiple dataset parameters may be supplied in one coordinate query and spatial coordinates are WGS84 EPSG:4326.
UPRN passed in q is documented as more precise than coordinate search for registered properties.
Entity responses include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point plus additional fields.
There is no batch endpoint; per-property requests should use polite rate limiting, while hundreds of properties should use bulk downloads.
Bulk dataset formats include CSV, JSON, GeoJSON where applicable, and Parquet.
Entity endpoints support json/html/geojson, reference filtering, offset pagination and prebuilt next/prev/first/last links.
LIDAR_Tiles_Catalogues FeatureServer is official and uses spatial reference EPSG:27700.
LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Extents layer 0 is a polygon feature layer with max record count 2000, JSON/GeoJSON/PBF query formats and standardized queries.
DTM layer fields include filename, os_ref, sd_flown and ed_flown.
DTM layer fields include pt_count, pt_spacing, intensity, returns, classified and gps_time.
DTM layer fields include transform, geoid, filepath, year, supplied, latest and polygon_id.
Exact OGC collection LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents is in EPSG:27700 and exposes filename, tilename, polygon_id, resolution, year, od_dtm_fn, sd_flown and ed_flown queryables.
Persistent DTM 1m WCS 2.0.1 is the raw-elevation transport and the documented NoData sentinel is -3.4028235e+38.
DTM Time Stamped Extents describes survey capture date, DTM resolution and transformation models; current service time extent reaches 2022.
Current OS Terrain 50 Version Date is July 2026; the product covers all Great Britain and is free OpenData.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July and is maintained through an integrated 3-to-5-year flying programme.
National ASCII/GML supply uses 2,858 ten-kilometre tiles arranged into 55 one-hundred-kilometre grid folders and requires no registration.
Each grid tile is 10km by 10km, identified from the National Grid reference of its south-west corner, with 200 by 200 pixels at 50m spacing.
Height values represent pixel centres; rows run west-to-east and successive rows move 50m south; values are supplied to the nearest 0.1m.
Grid delivery includes .asc height data, .gml metadata bridge, .prj CRS definition, .asc.aux.xml styling statistics and per-tile Metadata XML.
Per-tile metadata identifies British National Grid EPSG:27700 and vertical Ordnance Datum Newlyn EPSG:5701 and records earliest/latest flying dates.
OS Terrain 50 grid has verified 4m RMSE; the DTM models bare earth and removes buildings and vegetation while source grid/contours are interpolated from a TIN.
OpenData downloads endpoint supports fileName, format, subformat and area filters; TQ is a valid area value and redirect can return HTTP 307 for exactly one match.
